summary: Reviewed StationsView.tsx against all four review dimensions (maintainability, best practices, performance, future context). The useDebounce refactor is idiomatic and correct — hook integration, deps arrays, and type safety are all sound.
The _macro suffix strip (.replace(/_macro$/, '')) is correctly anchored to end-of-string; item.macro is non-optional in StationData so the call is safe without a null guard.

Identified one medium-priority improvement candidate: a double-fetch pattern when debouncedSearch/debouncedClassSearch change while offset > 0. Because fetchStations depends on both buildFilter (which depends on debouncedSearch) and offset, two sequential fetches fire. There is no AbortController to cancel the stale-offset request, leaving a narrow race window. This is a consequence of the AC3-specified separate offset-reset effect and does not produce incorrect final state under normal latency, but is worth addressing in a follow-up.
No blocking issues found. All six acceptance criteria remain met. Verdict: PASS.

comments.note: src/components/StationsView.tsx — double-fetch pattern: when debouncedSearch or debouncedClassSearch changes while offset > 0, two fetchStations calls are triggered in rapid succession. The first carries the stale offset (new filter + old page), the second carries offset 0 (correct). Without an AbortController or cleanup return in fetchStations, a slow first response could overwrite the correct second response (stale-closure race). Recommend adding AbortController / request-cancellation in a follow-up WP, or restructuring so offset and filter changes are handled in a single effect.

src/components/StationsView.tsx — the columns array and its accessor arrow functions are recreated on every render (not wrapped in useMemo). This is a pre-existing issue unrelated to this WP. If DataTable uses React.memo with shallow prop comparison, every parent render causes DataTable to re-render unnecessarily. Low risk given the current app scale, but worth memoizing in a future cleanup.

[documentation-forward] The _macro suffix-stripping behavior in the Type column is a user-visible change — the display value no longer matches the raw macro string stored in the save. This should be documented in the component's README or the project manifest (public-api.md / StationsView component description) so future developers understand the intentional display-vs-raw divergence.

No blocking issues found. useDebounce hook integration in StationsView.tsx is clean, idiomatic, and consistent with the hook's design. Deps arrays for buildFilter and fetchStations are exact. Type safety is solid throughout the modified code.
